title: Evaluation of local trace element status and 8-Iso-prostaglandin F2α concentrations in Tinea pedis
author: Miraloglu, Kurutas, et al.

steps.title: Collect skin scraping samples
steps.instruction: Using a sterile scalpel, scrape the edges of the interdigital lesion (and the corresponding non‑lesional area of the opposite foot) to obtain a moderate amount of tissue; place each sample into a sterile Petri dish.

steps.title: Perform direct KOH microscopy
steps.instruction: Transfer each scraping to a clean microscope slide, add 1–2 drops of 15 % KOH solution, cover with a cover slip, let stand at room temperature for 15–20 min, then examine at 40× magnification; record presence or absence of fungal elements.

steps.title: Inoculate Sabouraud’s dextrose agar
steps.instruction: Streak each scraping onto Sabouraud’s dextrose agar plates and incubate under standard fungal culture conditions.

steps.title: Homogenize samples in ice‑cold KCl
steps.instruction: Add two volumes (w/v) of 1.15 % ice‑cold KCl solution to each scraping, homogenize with a Heidolph 50110 R2R0 homogenizer, then centrifuge the homogenate at 39 880 g for 30 min at 4 °C using a Sorvall RC‑2B; collect the supernatant for analysis.

steps.title: Quantify 8‑iso‑PGF2α by ELISA
steps.instruction: Use a commercial ELISA kit to determine 8‑iso‑PGF2α concentrations in the supernatant according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Measure trace elements by AAS
steps.instruction: Determine selenium, zinc and copper concentrations in the supernatant using flame (Zn, Cu) and furnace (Se) atomic absorption spectrophotometry with Zeeman background correction.
